📝 Walkthrough ## Walkthrough The PR introduces foundational infrastructure across multiple ecosystems: new Python superfunctions packages (auth, db, oauth) with standardized Pydantic models and protocols; significant DataFn CLI improvements for Drizzle schema generation and package discovery; expanded core package exports; enhanced auth middleware with bearer token validation; refactored DB adapter imports; and complete example applications demonstrating FileFn and DataFn production workflows. ## Changes | Cohort / File(s) | Summary | |---|---| | **Python Core Auth Module**
`packages/python-core/superfunctions/auth/__init__.py` | New shared auth package with Pydantic models for `AuthSubject`, `AuthSession`, `AuthContext`, validation error handling, and runtime type guards/assertions for subject and session validation. | | **Python Core DB Module**
`packages/python-core/superfunctions/db/__init__.py`, `packages/python-core/superfunctions/db/errors.py`, `packages/python-core/superfunctions/db/types.py`, `packages/python-core/superfunctions/db/namespace.py` | New DB abstraction layer defining adapter Protocols, CRUD parameter types, query builders, error hierarchy, namespace management, and schema-related types for consistent database interactions. | | **Python Core OAuth Module**

`datafn/cli/src/utils/discover-packages.ts`, `datafn/cli/src/utils/discover-configs.ts`, `datafn/cli/src/utils/parse-library-init.ts`, `datafn/cli/src/commands/generate-schema.ts` | Redesigned package discovery to search nearest `node_modules` upward, support `libraryNames` metadata, resolve library entry points via new `resolveLibraryPackageEntryPoint` helper, and enhance config extraction with TypeScript assertion unwrapping. | | **DataFn CLI Tests**

`datafn/core/package.json`, `datafn/core/src/index.ts`, `datafn/core/src/types.ts`, `datafn/core/src/errors.ts`, `datafn/core/tsup.config.ts` | New subpath exports (`./types`, `./capabilities`, `./errors`, `./relations`, `./sort`), optional schema `version` field, `TRANSACTION_ROLLED_BACK` error code, and multi-entry tsup build configuration. | | **DataFn Server Context & Types**
`datafn/server/src/server.ts`, `datafn/server/src/core-types.ts`, `datafn/server/src/routes/status.ts`, `datafn/server/src/execution/search/cross-resource.ts`, `datafn/server/tsup.config.ts`, `datafn/server/src/__tests__/namespace-auto-wrap.test.ts` | Server configuration now accepts optional `context` (sync/async), widened `getActorId` contract to allow `undefined`, refactored core-types to re-export from `@datafn/core/*` subpaths, and added integration test for request-scoped context propagation. | | **DataFn Docs & Infrastructure**
`datafn/SECURITY.md`, `datafn/build.sh`, `datafn/bruno-datafn-server-test/opencollection.yml`, `datafn/bruno-datafn-server-test/sample mutation.yml` | Security specification document detailing rate limiting, DFQL validation, field-level permissions, multi-tenant isolation, WebSocket controls, and production checklist; build orchestration script for npm packages; Bruno HTTP test collection and sample mutation test. | | **Auth Middleware & Types**
`packages/auth/src/types.ts`, `packages/auth/src/middleware.ts`, `packages/auth/src/index.ts`, `packages/auth/src/__tests__/types.test.ts`, `packages/auth/src/middleware.test.ts` | New `AuthActorType`/`AuthSubject` modeling, `AuthSession` restructuring with subject field, bearer token extraction utilities, reusable `createBearerAuthMiddleware`, validation error handling, and comprehensive test coverage. | | **DB Adapter Updates**
`packages/db/package.json`, `packages/db/src/adapters/drizzle/index.ts`, `packages/db/src/adapters/drizzle/internal.ts` | Added `./adapters/drizzle` and `./adapters/memory` subpath exports; switched from dynamic to static `drizzle-orm` imports, removing optional dependency shim logic. | | **CLI & Discovery Utilities**

`botfn/bot-discord/...`, `botfn/discord-core/...`, `botfn/bot-slack/...`, `botfn/slack-core/...`, `botfn/github-integration/...`, `botfn/linear-integration/...`, `botfn/shared-types/...`, `botfn/persistence/...` | Version downgrades to `0.0.1`, added Vitest configs, new Slack events endpoint with signature validation, Drizzle ORM migration replacing D1 persistence, new database schema definitions, and standardized npm metadata fields. | | **FileFn Server**

`packages/python-core/tests/test_auth_http_types.py`, `packages/python-core/tests/test_oauth_modules.py` | New test suites covering auth session validation, cookie serialization, OpenAPI metadata, OAuth state consumption/replay, secret resolution errors, and consent/revocation storage validation. | ## Estimated code review effort 🎯 4 (Complex) | ⏱️ ~60 minutes ## Possibly related PRs - [`#38`](../../pull/38): Updates datafn/cli schema generation, package discovery, and codegen utilities with overlapping changes to Drizzle generation and CLI infrastructure. - [`#13`](../../pull/13): Modifies Drizzle/DB adapters, schema generation, and CLI discovery utilities that share code-level interactions with this PR's persistence and codegen changes. - [`#36`](../../pull/36): Adds and modifies the `@datafn/core` package (types, exports, runtime modules, build config) directly overlapping with core export changes in this PR. ## Suggested labels `Complex`, `multi-workspace`, `Python`, `TypeScript`, `CLI`, `schema-generation`, `examples`, `auth`, `database` --- > 🐰 *A rabbit hops through forests of code,* > *Python scripts and TypeScript nodes,* > *New schemas bloom, with OAuth's grace,* > *Examples flourish in every place!* > *The CLI learns to dance and sing,* > *A thousand packages on its wing!* 🚀

**Codebase verification**:  Verifies the impact on the overall codebase and identifies missing changes.

**Insights into your code**:  Ask any questions on your codebase within the pull request 

**Chat about your code** : Chat with the bot around your code. The more you chat, the smarter it gets.

**Issue Validation**:  Validates the PR against the linked issues and identifies other related issues

performed_via_github_app.description:
### Socket protects your app from malicious dependencies lurking in your open source supply chain.

Open source code makes up 90% of most codebases. It is critical to manage it effectively to reduce your security risk.

## Detect and block open source supply chain attacks

Security teams depend on Socket to prevent malicious open source dependencies from infiltrating their apps.

Socket dramatically improves your open source security posture by _detecting and blocking the attacks you don't expect_ – malware, install scripts, hidden code, typo-squatting, and more – which aren't caught by traditional vulnerability scanners.

- **Block malware** – Block emerging malware threats

- **Block typo-squatting** – Block malicious packages that differ in name by only a few characters, and recommend the correct package

- **Detect hidden code** – Detect obfuscated, minified, or hidden code

- **Detect privileged API usage** – Report when a dependency update introduces new risky API usage – filesystem, network, child_process, eval()

- **Detect suspicious updates** – Sudden inclusion of privileged APIs in patch or minor releases

Socket currently [supports 60 detections](https://socket.dev/npm/issue) in 5 categories: supply chain risk, quality, maintenance, known vulnerabilities, and license problems.

## Take charge of your dependency health

Socket improves security outcomes and reduces work for security teams by **surfacing actionable security information directly inline in GitHub** so developers are empowered to make better decisions.

- **Five minute deployment** – The easiest security product you'll ever deploy in your organization. Just install a GitHub app and you're done.

- **Provide security feedback directly on PRs** – Empower developers to solve security issues before they're deployed into production.

- **Automated security** – Spend security team resources auditing the highest-impact dependencies, instead of all or nothing.

## Socket detects what vulnerability scanners can’t

It's no longer sufficient to scan for known vulnerabilities (CVEs) and stop there. And yet, that's what the leading "supply chain security" products do, leaving you vulnerable.

It can take weeks or months for a CVE to be discovered, reported, and detected by tools. But in today's culture of fast development, a malicious dependency can be updated, merged, and running in production in days or even sometimes hours.

Defenders need a new approach to address emerging threats from malicious dependencies:

- **Maintainer intentionally added malware** – Rogue maintainer sabotaged his own open source package with 100M downloads/month, affecting companies such as Amazon AWS

- **Package hijacked and poisoned w/ cryptominers and password-stealing malware** – Deliberate malware introduced into multiple packages with 30M downloads/month each

- **Package hijacked to add backdoor targeting a specific organization** – Obfuscated malware added to a dependency which targeted a single company, went undetected for over a week, and made it into their production build

- **NPM package manager allowed anyone to publish new versions of any package** – Attackers could publish new versions of any NPM package without authorization _for multiple years_

Using third-party dependencies without proper vetting leaves you open to hacking, breaches, and assorted security misfortune.

body:
Greptile Summary

This is a large sync PR (106 files) bringing `next`-branch improvements into `dev` across BotFn, DataFn, FileFn, SearchFn, shared packages, and Python core. The vast majority of changes are clean — type refactors, codegen fixes, new OAuth modules, and example additions — but two behavioural bugs in the BotFn layer need addressing before merge. - **Connection pool leak** (`botfn/persistence/src/core.ts`): `postgres()` is called inside `createContext`, which runs on every tRPC request, creating an unbounded number of never-closed connection pools. - **Timing-unsafe HMAC comparison** (`botfn/slack-core/src/verify.ts`): The final `signature === hash` string equality leaks timing information and should be replaced with a constant-time byte comparison.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge after fixing the per-request connection pool leak and the timing-unsafe HMAC comparison in the BotFn layer. Two P1 findings remain: a connection pool leak that will exhaust Postgres connections under load, and a timing-unsafe HMAC comparison in the Slack signature verifier. The rest of the PR is well-structured and the stated test suite passes. `botfn/persistence/src/core.ts` (connection pool lifecycle) and `botfn/slack-core/src/verify.ts` (timing-safe comparison).

Security Review

 - **Timing-attack risk** (`botfn/slack-core/src/verify.ts` line 46): HMAC signature verification uses `===` string equality rather than a constant-time comparison, creating a timing oracle that allows gradual byte-by-byte guessing of a valid Slack signature. - No hardcoded secrets, injection vectors, or credential leakage found in the remaining changed files.

Important Files Changed

| Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | botfn/persistence/src/core.ts | Migrated from Cloudflare D1 to PostgreSQL/Drizzle ORM; introduces a per-request connection pool leak in `createContext`. | | botfn/slack-core/src/verify.ts | New Slack request signature verification using SubtleCrypto; final comparison uses timing-unsafe string equality instead of constant-time comparison. | | packages/db/src/adapters/drizzle/internal.ts | Replaced lazy dynamic import of `drizzle-orm` with static import; `getDrizzleSql()` null-guard is now unreachable dead code. | | packages/db/src/adapters/drizzle/index.ts | Switched from optional dynamic import of `drizzle-orm` to a static import, making drizzle-orm a hard load-time dependency and breaking the prior optional peer dep contract. | | datafn/cli/src/drizzle-codegen.ts | Added `emitInternalTables` for `__datafn_*` system tables, fixed epoch column type per dialect, and improved `default` serialization with `JSON.stringify`. | | packages/auth/src/middleware.ts | Added `extractBearerToken`, `extractBearerTokenFromHeader`, and `createBearerAuthMiddleware` helpers; hardened `resourceIds` access against undefined. | | packages/auth/src/types.ts | Added `AuthSubject`, `AuthContext`, `AuthContextProvider`, runtime predicates `isAuthSession`/`isAuthSubject`, and made `resourceIds` optional on `AuthSession`. | | datafn/server/src/core-types.ts | Replaced local type redeclarations with direct re-exports from `@datafn/core` subpath exports, eliminating duplication and TS2709 workarounds. | | packages/python-core/superfunctions/oauth/flow.py | New modular OAuth flow contracts: start/callback/refresh/disconnect models, service config, and hook protocols; well-structured with Pydantic models. | | botfn/persistence/src/schema.ts | New Drizzle PostgreSQL schema for `issues` and `discord_threads`, replacing implicit D1 DDL; column names aligned with ORM camelCase mappings. |

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Client participant Hono as Hono (createPersistenceApp) participant tRPC as tRPC fetchRequestHandler participant createContext participant PG as postgres.js pool Client->>Hono: POST /trpc/createIssue Hono->>tRPC: fetchRequestHandler(req, createContext) tRPC->>createContext: createContext(env) ← called per request createContext->>PG: postgres(DATABASE_URL) ← NEW pool created every time PG-->>createContext: db createContext-->>tRPC: { db } tRPC->>PG: db.insert(issues).values(...) PG-->>tRPC: result tRPC-->>Hono: response Hono-->>Client: 200 OK Note over PG: Pool is never closed — leaks accumulate ```
Prompt To Fix All With AI `````markdown This is a comment left during a code review. Path: botfn/persistence/src/core.ts Line: 89-93 Comment: **New connection pool created on every request** `createContext` is invoked by `fetchRequestHandler` once per tRPC call (see line 393: `createContext: () => createContext(c.env)`). Each invocation calls `postgres(env.DATABASE_URL)`, which constructs a new `postgres.js` connection pool that is never closed. Under any sustained load this will exhaust the PostgreSQL `max_connections` limit, and even at idle each request leaves orphaned pool objects. The pool should be instantiated once at server startup — for example by calling `createPersistenceApp` with a pre-built `db` argument, or by lazily initialising a module-level singleton on first request. How can I resolve this? If you propose a fix, please make it concise. --- This is a comment left during a code review. Path: botfn/slack-core/src/verify.ts Line: 46 Comment: **Timing-unsafe HMAC signature comparison** The final comparison `signature === hash` uses a standard string equality operator, which short-circuits on the first differing character and leaks the number of matching bytes through response-time variations. For HMAC-based request authentication (the Slack signing scheme), this creates a practical timing oracle. Replace the string comparison with a constant-time byte comparison: ```suggestion const sigBuf = enc.encode(signature.startsWith('v0=') ? signature.slice(3) : signature); const hashBuf = new Uint8Array(signed); if (sigBuf.length !== hashBuf.length) return false; let diff = 0; for (let i = 0; i < hashBuf.length; i++) { diff |= (sigBuf[i] ?? 0) ^ hashBuf[i]; } return diff === 0; ``` Alternatively use Node's `crypto.timingSafeEqual` if running under Node.js compatibility. How can I resolve this? If you propose a fix, please make it concise. --- This is a comment left during a code review. Path: packages/db/src/adapters/drizzle/internal.ts Line: 52-58 Comment: **`getDrizzleSql()` null-guard is now dead code** `drizzleSql` is imported with a static `import { sql as drizzleSql } from 'drizzle-orm'`, so it is always a function at module load time (or the module fails to resolve before this guard is ever reached). The `if (!drizzleSql)` branch can never be true, and the informative error message will never surface. If `drizzle-orm` is absent, consumers will see a bare `Cannot find module 'drizzle-orm'` error instead of the helpful message. The guard can be removed, or the function inlined. How can I resolve this? If you propose a fix, please make it concise. --- This is a comment left during a code review. Path: packages/db/src/adapters/drizzle/index.ts Line: 26 Comment: **Static import makes `drizzle-orm` a hard dependency** The original code used a dynamic `await import('drizzle-orm')` with a `try/catch` so that `@superfunctions/db` could be installed without `drizzle-orm` (the previous comment explicitly called it an "optional peer dep"). The new `import * as drizzleOps from 'drizzle-orm'` makes the package a required module at load time: any consumer that installs `@superfunctions/db` without `drizzle-orm` will now get an immediate `Cannot find module` error when the adapter module is first imported, even if they never instantiate the Drizzle adapter. Consider reverting to a dynamic import or gating behind a factory function, or explicitly promote `drizzle-orm` to a required `peerDependency` in `packages/db/package.json` so the expectation is declared upfront. How can I resolve this? If you propose a fix, please make it concise. `````
